Hot tub removal is not a simple DIY task, it requires careful planning and attention to safety. Without proper precautions, you could risk injury or property damage.

items: Hot tubs are powered by electricity. Ensure power is disconnected by a certified electrician before starting removal.
Hot tubs are heavy and bulky. Improper removal can damage decking, landscaping, or flooring.
Hot tubs contain water and chemicals that need proper disposal to avoid harming the environment.
Heavy-duty lifting tools, dollies, and straps.
Protective gloves, safety glasses, and footwear.
Proper disposal containers for water and chemicals.

blocks.text: Spa Demolition: What You Need to Know

c: Sometimes your hot tub needs more than just removal, and it requires complete spa demolition. This is especially true for old or damaged units that can’t be reused.

items: Drain all water and disconnect electrical and plumbing connections.
Wear protective equipment to prevent injury.
Remove cabinet panels and components to reduce weight.
Use proper tools to separate structural parts.
Transport pieces using dollies or heavy-lifting equipment.
Take care to protect the surrounding landscaping.
Properly dispose of foam, wiring, wood, and plastics.
Recycle materials whenever possible.
